unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD AND CITY

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a comprehensive project about the attractions, recreational places, services, and transport in their neighbourhood and city. The project will include identifying key attractions such as parks, historical sites, museums, or shopping areas, and describing how these places contribute to the lifestyle of the community. Additionally, students will explore the essential services in their area, such as schools, hospitals, libraries, and community centres, and explain their significance in meeting the needs of residents. Transportation will also be a focus, with students checking the available options, including public transport, walking and cycling routes, and road networks, and discussing simply and talking about them. Students will design a visual presentation to accompany their project, such as a map or infographic, highlighting the locations of attractions, services, and transportation routes. They are encouraged to add photos, drawings, or symbols to make their work more engaging. Alongside the visual component, students will simply write a reflection on how these aspects contribute to making their neighbourhood and city liveable, discussing any challenges they observe, such as traffic or limited services, and proposing solutions for improvement. Finally, students will present their projects to the class, using their visuals to support a clear and engaging explanation. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics and a marking scheme. bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood and city with its components such as attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood and city'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a bus, a car, a guide, to travel, to go, to see and so on'' and also some structures such as ''It was beautiful, wasn’t it. I was there last year.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a paper map or a digital map, a large picture of sightseeing places could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the map and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students to talk about attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in English through an interactive and discussion-based activity by using the target vocabulary. Objective: To talk about attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in English through a discussion-based activity by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Neighbourhood and City Debate The teacher divides students into small groups and gives each group a set of vocabulary cards related to attractions, services, and transportation (e.g., gallery, embassy). Each group must select one item from each category (e.g., an attraction, a service, and a mode of transportation) and argue why their chosen combination creates the best neighbourhood or city. For example: ''A gallery attracts tourists and supports local culture, an embassy provides essential international services, and trams are efficient and environmentally friendly.'' After presenting their arguments, the teacher provides feedback on the use of language with the target vocabulary, clarity of ideas, and communication skills, encouraging students to use advanced descriptive language. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students use the language target vocabulary related to attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in English through an analytical and vocabulary-focused activity by using the target vocabulary. Objective: To understand and analyse attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in a text in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 2: Detailed Reading and Analysis The teacher provides students an article about urban development according to their age and language level and discusses topics such as the integration of historical sites into modern cities, the role of public services, and advancements in transportation. Students work individually to read the text and underline key vocabulary related to attractions, services, and transportation (e.g., monument preservation, public facilities, and sustainable transit systems). After reading, they answer detailed comprehension questions such as: ''How does the text describe the benefits of sustainable transportation?''. Finally, students share their answers in pairs, and the teacher provides feedback on comprehension accuracy and vocabulary use. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To identify and talk about neighbourhood attractions in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Neighbourhood Attractions and Adjectives Matching Game The teacher provides students with two sets of cards: one with pictures or names of attractions (e.g., a park, a castle, a square) and another with adjectives (e.g., relaxing, historical, amazing). Students work in pairs to match the attractions with suitable adjectives (e.g., a park—relaxing, a castle—historical). After completing the matches, the teacher points to a card and asks simple questions like ''What is this?'' or ''How is it?'' Students respond with short answers, such as ''It’s a park'' or ''It’s relaxing.'' The pair with the most correct matches and answers wins the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To talk about attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 2: Vocabulary Sorting Game The teacher gives students a list of mixed words, such as a castle, a fire department, and a ferry, related to attractions, services, and transportation. Students work in pairs to sort the words into three categories: Attractions, Services, and Transportation. After sorting, the teacher points to a word and asks questions such as, ''What is this?'' or ''Where can you find it?''. Students answer with simple phrases, such as ''It’s a castle'' or ''In the city.'' Then the teacher asks other students to say the words in full sentences. After each answer, the teacher provides feedback, correcting any mistakes and praising accurate responses. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
